stemBlocks.value: OPQ is a triangle in which ARB and AOQ are straight lines. B is the midpoint of PQ, R is the midpoint of AB, R lies on OP with OR : RP = 1 : 3, OP = 4a and OQ = 8b. Find, in terms of a and/or b in simplest form: (iv) PQ, (v) PR, (vi) RB.
Think first: Take O as origin: once you have the position vectors of P, Q, R and B, every answer is a subtraction.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p283-q06 from workbook page 283.

solutionSteps.instruction: Subtract the position vectors of P and Q.
Use the ratio OR : RP = 1 : 3 to locate R on OP.

contentBlocks.value: OR is one of four equal parts of OP, so OR = (1/4)(4a)

solutionSteps.instruction: Find PR by subtracting the position vectors of P and R.
Find B, the midpoint of PQ, using the midpoint rule.
Subtract OR from OB to get RB.

strategyBlocks.value: Write PQ as OQ − OP, use OR : RP = 1 : 3 to get OR = (1/4)OP = a, find B as the midpoint of PQ, then subtract to get RB.

whyThisWorks.value: Choosing O as the origin turns every point into a position vector, and the vector from one point to another is always 'position of the finish minus position of the start'. A ratio of 1 : 3 along OP means OP is cut into four equal pieces, so OR is a quarter of OP. The midpoint rule is simply the average of the two end position vectors, which places B exactly halfway along PQ.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading OR : RP = 1 : 3 as OR = (1/3)OP instead of (1/4)OP.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading OR : RP = 1 : 3 as OR = (1/3)OP instead of (1/4)OP.
